The read is service-role (RLS bypassed) and keyed on a caller-supplied venueId, so any authenticated caller could read any venue's capacity by submitting an oversized expectedAttendance. AC-2 forbids exactly this shape of disclosure, so it was fixed in the same function.

NON-ATOMIC REJECTION: POST inserted the artist booking_requests row (base :312) BEFORE the availability gate (base :342). The same applied to the 401 requester check and the three 422 policy checks that also sat after the insert. A rejection that still writes is not a rejection, so this was fixed by hoisting the whole venue-side validation block ahead of the first insert.

residual_findings_left_deliberately.finding: The canonical availability contract and the pre-existing approved-booking conflict check in the SAME function use two different notions of 'that day'. isVenueEventDateBlocked derives the UTC calendar day (toAvailabilityCalendarDay). The approved-booking check uses the window [requestedStart, requestedStart + 1 day). An approved booking earlier on the same UTC day as a 19:00 request is therefore NOT detected as a conflict.
residual_findings_left_deliberately.why_not_fixed_here: Fixing it changes existing conflict behaviour for a check no acceptance criterion covers, and the correct window depends on whether a booking request is a point-in-time performance or a multi-hour/multi-day occupancy. Guessing would be a second unrequested derivation. This is precisely the 'two surfaces come to disagree' risk the brief names, so it is pinned by a test rather than silently normalised.
residual_findings_left_deliberately.evidence: Test 'documents the divergence between the two day-window derivations' — an approved booking at 18:00Z against a 19:00Z request currently returns 200 and inserts.
residual_findings_left_deliberately.recommended: A follow-up decision should settle whether booking-request conflict detection is a calendar-day question or an interval question, then make both checks use one derivation. EVENTS-002-D1.title: A venue availability block read error fails OPEN at the booking-request boundary, and is logged rather than swallowed
EVENTS-002-D1.decision: isVenueEventDateBlocked returns { blocked, error, date }. On `blocked === true` the route rejects with 409. On a truthy `error` with blocked false, the route proceeds (fails open) and logs via console.error. The contract is not modified and no second derivation is introduced.
EVENTS-002-D1.divergence_from_venue_lane: HF-VENUE-004-BOOKING-RECEIVING next_steps[1] asks the receiving lane to 'treat a truthy error from the helper as fail-closed (reject the request) rather than passing the booking through'. EVENTS-002 deliberately did NOT follow that instruction. This is flagged for the venue lane to ratify or override; it is a contract-usage policy question the venue lane owns, not an events-lane preference.
reasoning: CONSISTENCY, and this is the decisive argument: both PRE-EXISTING checks in validateVenueAvailability already fail open on a read error. The venue_profiles read destructures only `{ data: venue }` and discards the error, so a failed capacity read yields capacity 0 and no rejection. The venue_booking_requests count destructures only `{ count }`, so a failed read yields undefined and `count || 0` is 0, no rejection. Making only the NEW check fail closed would make it the odd one out, and a transient database error would reject requests that the two established checks in the same function would have allowed.
BLAST RADIUS: fail-closed here rejects 100% of booking requests across ALL venues on a transient read error, converting a brief infrastructure blip into a total denial of business.

SEVERITY: a booking REQUEST is not a confirmed booking. The venue manager still reviews and approves it, and VENUE-005's reservation conflict engine is the actual double-booking guard. A missed advisory block yields a request the venue can decline, not a double-booked room.
EVENTS-002-D1.counter_consideration: The venue lane's instinct is defensible: a block that exists but cannot be read is a silent bypass, and the helper's own lib test describes the propagated error as existing 'so callers can fail closed'. If the venue lane prefers fail-closed, the correct change is a contract-level policy decision applied consistently to all three checks, not a one-off flip in this route.
EVENTS-002-D1.evidence: Test 'fails open on a block-read error and logs it instead of swallowing it' injects a read error and asserts 200, one venue insert, and an exact console.error call. The behaviour is pinned, not merely asserted in a comment.
EVENTS-002-D1.owner: venue (contract) with events (consumer), adjudicated by the orchestrator
